dedupe_keys.name: wia australian repeater and beacon directory

description: The Wireless Institute of Australia publishes the Australian repeater directory as downloadable files, with a separate beacon list. The directory is updated about twice a year when there are enough changes, and each file carries a date stamp; submission guidelines for updates are on the last page of the listing. The download includes a Google Earth KMZ file that the page says is generated automatically and kept up to date with the ACMA database, showing the location of every amateur, CB and marine repeater in Australia with frequency information, filterable by service. The page also points to the linked networks used by repeaters, such as IRLP, EchoLink, D-STAR, P25, DMR and System Fusion, and to a free repeater app. Access is free by download from the page; no licence is stated. Caveats: the listing is updated only about twice a year, and details depend on submissions and the regulator's database. Coverage is Australia. It supports emergency response and communication resilience studies, such as mapping radio repeaters that serve as backup links in bushfires and floods; related records are the ÖVSV repeater database and HamnetDB.
